stories.headline: A powerful nor'easter storm battered the US Northeast, causing widespread blackouts and flooding
stories.body: A powerful nor'easter storm brought flooding and power outages across the northeastern United States on Saturday. Travel suffered immediate disruption as airlines cancelled more than 400 flights by Saturday afternoon. Electricity grids also failed across several states. Power outages affected over 88,000 homes and businesses as of Saturday afternoon. Poweroutage.com reported that 101,674 homes and businesses were without power as of 1:15 p.m. Saturday. This outage covered areas from Massachusetts to Maryland. In New York City, estimated rainfall forecasts doubled to six inches on Saturday. The heavy rain caused power outages for about 22,000 customers in the city. The governors of New York and New Jersey declared states of emergency in counties expected to suffer the worst impact, including New York City. New York Governor Kathy Hochul issued a strong warning to residents. Hochul said, "Anyone who goes in or near the water this weekend is literally gambling with their life". Officials in New York also warned of wind gusts reaching up to 55 mph, or 86 km/h, throughout the weekend. Coastal regions prepared for high waters and rising seas. Senior forecaster Bob Oravec of the US Weather Prediction Center said storm surges were expected to raise ocean levels by three feet along the coasts of New Jersey and New York. In Sea Bright, Mayor Brian Kelly said he expected street flooding to reach up to 6ft. Kelly compared the threat to an "Irene-scale flooding event". In Manasquan, New Jersey, officials issued a voluntary evacuation order for residents living in low-lying areas. Private property also suffered damage from the strong winds. Kenny Formica, a marina owner in Surf City, New Jersey, reported that a customer's 25ft boat worth $150,000 blew off its lift during the storm. Transit networks and major events faced widespread cancellations. The Long Island Rail Road suspended service on its Long Beach Branch due to flooding on Saturday. Musician Ed Sheeran cancelled scheduled concerts in Massachusetts on Friday and Saturday because of the weather. A professional football match between Red Bull New York and St Louis City SC was also cancelled due to the storm. In sports, the Boston Red Sox rescheduled the last game of their series against the Chicago Cubs. The game was moved to Sunday afternoon in Florida.

stories.headline: US President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to shipping
stories.body: US President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping within seven days. The strategic waterway has been effectively closed to shipping since war broke out between the US, Israel, and Iran in late February. Strategic stretches of Yemen's Red Sea coast, including the port of Mokha, were seized by Yemen's Houthis. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi had proposed a seven-day plan. The plan required the US to lift its naval blockade, waive oil sanctions, and agree to a ceasefire covering Lebanon in exchange for reopening the strait. Araghchi said that Tehran would wait for the definitive views of mediators regarding Trump's comments before making a decision. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told CBS that Iran would permit UN nuclear inspectors to enter the country if the US accepts its proposal. Pezeshkian also told Fox News that Iran signed an agreement based on a June memorandum of understanding and remains willing to move forward. Under that June agreement, Iran promised not to seek a nuclear weapon and to reopen the strait in return for US blockade relief and eased sanctions. But Trump posted an image on Truth Social showing the Strait of Hormuz labelled as "Trump Strait". The Wall Street Journal reported that Trump told aides he expects to resume a bombing campaign against Iran after US midterm elections in November. Saudi Arabia expressed concern that Iran's deal was a bilateral agreement between Iran and Oman rather than involving Gulf states as joint signatories.

stories.headline: US and China agreed to selective tariff relief and an AI communication channel after Washington summit
stories.body: Chinese President Xi Jinping concluded a three-day summit visit to Washington with US President Donald Trump on Friday. Following the meeting, the United States and China agreed to reduce tariffs on $30 billion of non-sensitive goods in each direction. The tariff reductions cover US exports such as agricultural goods, wood, and cosmetics, as well as US imports including small appliances, toys, and decorations. Both countries also agreed to extend their trade truce by two months beyond its scheduled November 10 expiration date. On technology, the White House said on Friday that both nations agreed to establish a bilateral communication channel for artificial intelligence incidents. Trump announced that his administration would rename artificial intelligence as "super intelligence" or SI in official communications. China's Foreign Ministry said that Beijing respects Washington's position and phrasing switch. But Trump told reporters at the White House that the US should not integrate AI initiatives with China because the US leads China by a lot. Trump said upon departing that the US is not going to put brakes on AI development. During broader diplomatic exchanges, Chinese Vice President Han Zheng indirectly asked the US at the UN General Assembly to respect the sovereignty of Iran and Cuba. Trump had previously warned Xi against supplying shoulder-mounted air-defence missile launchers to Iran and helping Iran evade oil sanctions.

stories.headline: Lethal air strikes struck Ukraine and Russia as fighting and infrastructure destruction escalated
stories.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday that Russia is escalating the war every single day. Recent Russian and Ukrainian strikes killed at least 16 people over 24 hours across both countries and occupied territories. A wave of Russian strikes hit various regions across Ukraine. Strikes on Kyiv killed seven people and forced a halt to production at ArcelorMittal, Ukraine's largest steelmaker. Russia's Defence Ministry said that its forces struck a cargo vessel carrying military supplies near Odesa. In Russia, a Ukrainian drone attack in the southern Krasnodar region killed three people and damaged the Ilsky oil refinery. Zelensky said that Ukrainian air defences are intercepting 55 percent of jet-powered drones launched by Russia. Speaking at the UN General Assembly, Zelensky said that Russia is using nationals from 47 countries on the battlefield through deception. US President Donald Trump said that 25,000 people died in the war last month, after 32,000 deaths the previous month and 33,000 two months prior. Diplomatic tensions remain high. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov vowed that Moscow's military objectives will be achieved. Lavrov accused Europe at the UN General Assembly of trying to thwart peace talks supported by the Trump administration. Zelensky said that Washington proposed a meeting of Russian, Ukrainian, and US officials in the United Arab Emirates.

stories.headline: A Pakistani Taliban suicide attack killed at least 11 people near a police checkpost in Dera Ismail Khan
stories.body: A suicide bomber rammed an explosives-laden tractor-trolley into the Aman Mela police checkpost in Pakistan's Dera Ismail Khan district. At least 11 to 12 people were killed in the suicide attack. Two customs and excise officials were among those killed in the bombing. Around 30 people, mostly security personnel and passersby, were injured in the blast. The Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan claimed responsibility for the suicide attack in a statement. The militant group had ended its ceasefire with the Pakistani government in November 2022. Pakistan has repeatedly accused Kabul of allowing Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan members to operate from Afghan soil, an accusation Afghan authorities deny. The bombing occurred two days after border clashes between Pakistan and Afghanistan killed at least 13 Afghan Taliban fighters. At the same time, international powers are participating in peace efforts. China, Turkey, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia are participating in mediation efforts to secure peace between Pakistan and Afghanistan.

stories.headline: Pope Leo XIV celebrated a massive open-air Mass in central Paris during a historic papal visit
stories.body: Pope Leo XIV celebrated an outdoor Mass in Paris during the first papal visit to France in two decades. The four-day trip marks the first official papal visit to the country in nearly two decades. The Pope held Mass along the Avenue des Champs-Elysees with an estimated 800,000 people attending. The Vatican estimated that 700,000 people turned out for the outdoor Mass at Place de la Concorde in Paris. About 14,500 police officers, gendarmes, military personnel, and firefighters were deployed to secure the event. Attendees included Brigitte Macron, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu, far-right leader Marine Le Pen, and LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault. French President Emmanuel Macron did not attend, represented instead by his wife Brigitte. Born Robert Prevost in Chicago in 1955, Pope Leo XIV is the first US-born pontiff. During his visit, he visited the Maison Bakhita center to meet migrants and volunteers supporting refugees. He also cautioned against "losing our humanity amid a paradise of machines" regarding artificial intelligence. The visit comes after a 2021 inquiry found clergy or lay members abused about 330,000 minors over seven decades. An INSEE report showed only 25% of French 18-to-49-year-olds identify as Catholic, down from 43% a decade earlier.

stories.headline: Election Commission of India announced revision rule changes amid political protests and misconduct claims
stories.body: The Election Commission of India faced growing political backlash over its Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Political opposition mounted as Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray announced a joint public march with Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray. The protest is planned in Mumbai on October 4, 2026, against the Special Intensive Revision process. Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray also backed calls for protests in Mumbai against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar beginning October 2. Raj Thackeray called the Election Commission of India a wing of the BJP. He accused Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of committing fraud under the SIR process. Serious allegations against Kumar also emerged from a former official. Former Kerala Chief Secretary Jiji Thomson alleged that Kumar asked him on a flight in 2016 whether he was interested in contesting the 2019 Lok Sabha election as a BJP candidate. Following this allegation, Cockroach Janta Party leader Abhijeet Dipke called for Kumar's resignation. The Cockroach Janta Party launched its 'Election Commission Thik Karo' campaign. The party cited the exclusion of more than 13 crore names from draft electoral rolls across 30 states and Union Territories during the Special Intensive Revision. Kumar became the 26th Chief Election Commissioner of India in February 2025. Internal tensions within the commission were also reported. The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi raised objections on record at least 14 times over 10 months. Their objections concerned decisions made regarding the Special Intensive Revision without their knowledge. But the Election Commission stated on Saturday that decisions concerning the revision had received unanimous approval from Kumar, Sandhu, and Joshi. In response to concerns, the Election Commission announced operational changes. The commission announced measures including doorstep collection of documents from voters who have been issued notices during the revision. The Election Commission also announced that a committee including an independent expert from an IIT or IIIT will review ECINET. Meanwhile, government allies defended the election body. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu said that the Election Commission's clarification reaffirmed the integrity and credibility of India's constitutional institutions. LJP (Ram Vilas) chief Chirag Paswan questioned why opposition parties remain silent about electoral processes in states where they have formed governments.

stories.headline: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar criticized Pakistan over terrorism in UN General Assembly speech
stories.body: Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar criticized Pakistan during his address at the United Nations General Assembly. Jaishankar described Pakistan as a 'serial practitioner of terrorism' during his speech at the 81st UN General Assembly session. Jaishankar called for targeting and exposing the financial networks that sustain terrorism. He also cited Prime Minister Narendra Modi's earlier remarks highlighting how regional conflicts in West Asia disrupt global energy security, maritime trade, and supply chains. Additionally, Jaishankar said that the war in Ukraine was nearing its fifth year, and said India supports a two-state solution to achieve durable peace in the Israel-Palestine conflict. Prime Minister Narendra Modi skipped the UN General Assembly session in 2026, marking the fifth time Jaishankar delivered India's National Statement. During the assembly, Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif called Kashmir Pakistan's 'jugular vein' and accused India of human rights violations. Sharif credited US President Donald Trump for intervening to end the India-Pakistan military conflict last year. Trump reshared an 87-second video clip of Sharif's speech on Truth Social without adding comment. But India rejected claims of US mediation, asserting that Operation Sindoor was paused after a request from Pakistan's Director General of Military Operations. India had launched Operation Sindoor on May 7 last year against terror infrastructure following an attack in Pahalgam on April 22 that killed 26 civilians. On maritime safety, eighteen Indians have been among seafarers killed during attacks linked to conflicts in Ukraine and West Asia. India joined Liberia and 23 other partner nations in a global initiative to oppose attacks on commercial shipping in international waterways.
